cards.title: Use Published Claude Artifacts as High-Authority Parasite SEO Hosts
cards.summary: Publish a Claude-generated article as a public artifact on claude.ai to borrow the root domain's authority and rank fast for brand and bottom-of-funnel terms.
cards.use_when: You need a brand-owned page or landing page to appear on Google quickly — e.g., brand-name searches, local SEO terms, or bottom-of-funnel keywords — and building a real page on your own site would take days.
steps: Prepare a single source document containing all your marketing material: homepage copy (navigation and footer included is fine), product descriptions, and as many testimonials and reviews as you can gather. Keep this doc updated so you can reuse it.

Paste the whole document into Claude with a prompt like: 'This is the homepage of my product. Write a thorough article about why my product is great, why it is proven, trustworthy, reputable and the best in [category].' For a keyword variant: 'This is my bottom-of-funnel keyword and my brand — write a thorough landing page for why my brand is the best solution for this keyword.'

Claude produces an artifact — a standalone editable content piece. Review it, then click the publish button. Claude warns the artifact becomes accessible to anyone on the internet and potentially visible in search results, while the chat stays private.

The artifact lives at claude.ai/public/artifacts/<unique-id> — a subfolder under a root domain the source cites at 66/100 domain authority. Subfolders inherit root-domain strength better than subdomains, which is why this can outrank weaker pages.
To help indexing, share the artifact link with people and ask them to click it; the source notes clicks help URLs get indexed.
Use this as a placeholder that ranks while you build the real page on your own site, then let the real page take over.
Track the artifact URL's position for your target keywords alongside your own site pages so you can see when the real page replaces it.
caveats: The 66/100 domain authority figure and the '5-hour' ranking claim come from the source and a cited YouTube video (Jesper Nissen) plus a commenter's local-SEO anecdote — treat these as examples, not guarantees.
Works best on low-competition, low-volume or local keywords; competitive terms are harder.
Publishing rules, the publish button location, and whether public artifacts stay indexed can change — verify the current Claude interface.
You do not control claude.ai; the artifact could be removed or deindexed, so never rely on it as your only brand asset.

cards.title: Prioritize Bottom-of-Funnel SEO Pages Over Cold-Audience Content
cards.summary: The source argues bottom-of-funnel pages targeting people ready to act convert far better than skyscraper-style top-of-funnel articles aimed at cold searchers.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to allocate SEO effort — e.g., choosing which landing pages or keyword pages to build next for your store.
steps: Classify each target keyword by buyer intent: bottom-of-funnel keywords are searched by people looking to take action with a brand (e.g., 'best [category] for [specific need]', local service terms), while top-of-funnel keywords attract cold searchers who may not convert.
Prioritize standalone bottom-of-funnel pages on your own site — the source says this is the best form of bottom-of-funnel SEO even though a proper page takes a day or two to build.
While the real page is being built, publish an interim Claude artifact targeting the same keyword so something ranks in the meantime (see the parasite-SEO card).
Avoid spending weeks on skyscraper-technique top-of-funnel articles if your goal is conversions from people ready to buy.
Reuse your existing marketing assets — homepage copy, reviews, testimonials — as the raw material so bottom-of-funnel pages can be produced quickly.
caveats: This is the presenter's opinion and a pitch for their own 'compact keywords' method; it is not an established universal rule.
Top-of-funnel content still has value for awareness and later demand; the source frames it as lower priority for conversion, not worthless.
Bottom-of-funnel keywords are often lower volume than broad terms.

cards.title: Exploit Relaxed Local Communities for Parasite SEO
cards.summary: Local subreddits and similar low-moderation communities let local businesses place links and posts that rank or drive traffic, unlike tightly-moderated national communities.
cards.use_when: Running local SEO or acquisition for a store with a physical or regional presence and looking for cheap ranking channels.
steps: Identify local subreddits and community forums tied to your city or region, where the source says moderation is often lax and linking rules are relaxed.
Check each community's rules before posting — the source notes mods in larger subreddits are sharper and actively prevent parasite SEO, while local mods may be 'asleep'.
Contribute a post or comment that naturally links to your store, landing page, or artifact, since direct links are what the big subreddits block.
Do this alongside publishing Claude artifacts for the same local keywords, since local niches are often non-competitive and rank easily.
Track referral traffic and ranking movement for the local terms you target to see which communities actually convert.
caveats: The source references a prior episode ('Local Subreddits Are Open for Parasite SEO', episode 642) for detail — the current text only summarizes it.
Moderation rules change; a community that allows links today may ban them tomorrow, and repeated link-dropping can get you banned.
Parasite-SEO tactics carry reputational and platform-policy risk; they are a short-term play, not a durable brand strategy.
